rationale: This contract has reasonable liability protections (capped at $95,000, mutual indemnification, appropriate disclaimer of consequential damages) that make it less risky than ultra-risky contracts. However, significant concerns remain: the disconnect between implementing SOC 2/PCI DSS controls and being responsible for certification, dependence on 15+ third-party financial APIs with no guarantees, and a 120-day warranty for rapidly-changing integrations. The $30,000 upfront payment and aggressive 5-month timeline add financial risk. With proper negotiations, this could become acceptable.
required_changes_to_accept: Reduce upfront payment to 20% ($19,000) or make it refundable if project doesn't reach first milestone
Add explicit budget ($15,000-25,000) for penetration testing remediation and security fixes
Reduce warranty period to 60 days due to frequent third-party API changes
Define 'material defects' vs 'minor defects' more precisely
Add provision that if more than 30% of financial institution integrations fail, Client can terminate with partial refund
Extend timeline to 6-7 months to account for third-party integration complexity
Clarify acceptance criteria with specific test cases and success metrics
Add mutual agreement requirement for what constitutes 'successful integration' milestone
Specify that compliance implementation is 'best effort' and auditor findings require change order
Split arbitration costs equally rather than each party bearing their own
Extend testing period to 20 business days (4 weeks) given platform complexity
